old_record.name: Pâtisserie Fabien Berteau
old_record.why: The pâtisserie address of Beaune. To order: the seasonal-fruit cheesecake, the chef's signature; macarons; the morning viennoiserie. Revised French classics and house-made ice cream. The tea room Le Garden opposite does an affordable lunch under a shaded summer terrace. Closed Wednesday.

old.name: Pinot Noir — the red of the Côte
old.label: WINE
old.hook: One grape, several hundred climats, a different wine every hundred metres
old.text: One grape, several hundred climats, a different wine every hundred metres EUR 25-200+ / bottle ESSENTIAL at table Dinner The entire red Côte d'Or is a single grape — Pinot Noir — read through several hundred named climats . Beaune's own appellation is overwhelmingly red: Les Grèves, Les Bressandes, Les Teurons, Champs Pimont, the upper-slope premier crus that climb behind the town. The lesson of Burgundy is that the variety is almost a constant and the ground is the variable. Taste it across the Côte by the glass at Loiseau des Vignes . Where Beaune 1er cru · the whole Côte d'Or

old.name: Chardonnay — and the Clos des Mouches
old.label: WINE
old.hook: The white grape of the world's greatest dry whites — Meursault, Puligny, Corton-Charlemagne
old.text: The white grape of the world's greatest dry whites — Meursault, Puligny, Corton-Charlemagne EUR 30-300+ / bottle ESSENTIAL at table Lunch / Dinner The Côte de Beaune is where Chardonnay became the benchmark white of the planet — Meursault, Puligny-Montrachet, Corton-Charlemagne, all within a short drive south and north of town. Beaune itself makes one celebrated white: the Clos des Mouches , a premier cru owned in its white part by Joseph Drouhin. Buy the village wines at the Saturday market vignerons; taste the crus at the négociant cellars. Where Côte de Beaune

old.name: The climat — Beaune's 42 premier crus
old.label: TERROIR
old.hook: 42 premier crus, zero grand crus — a singular ratio
old.text: 42 premier crus, zero grand crus — a singular ratio — — — A climat is a named, mapped parcel of vines with its own history and rank — the unit the Cistercian monks invented by walking the slope for centuries. Beaune's appellation holds 42 of them at premier cru and not a single grand cru: more than three-quarters of the appellation classed at the upper tier, yet no crown. The town put its ambition into the trade. The whole system was inscribed by UNESCO in 2015. Read it at the Cité des Climats et Vins . Where the slope west of the ramparts

old.name: Kir — Aligoté & crème de cassis
old.label: APÉRITIF
old.hook: A measure of cassis, five of cold Aligoté — named for a priest-mayor
old.text: A measure of cassis, five of cold Aligoté — named for a priest-mayor EUR 4-7 WALK-IN Apéritif The Burgundian apéritif: one part crème de cassis under four or five of cold Bourgogne Aligoté, the sharp third white grape whose acidity carries the sweet blackcurrant liqueur. Named for Félix Kir, the Resistance priest and mayor of Dijon from 1945 to 1968, who poured it at every civic reception. Swap the Aligoté for Crémant and it becomes a Kir Royale. The cassis itself has its museum 18 km north, the Cassissium at Nuits-Saint-Georges. Where every café

old.name: Crémant de Bourgogne
old.label: SPARKLING
old.hook: Méthode traditionnelle, AOC since 1975 — Burgundy's everyday bubble
old.text: Méthode traditionnelle, AOC since 1975 — Burgundy's everyday bubble EUR 12-25 / bottle WALK-IN All day Burgundy's sparkling wine, made by the same bottle-fermented method as Champagne — minimum nine months on the lees — and an AOC in its own right since 1975. Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Aligoté and Gamay are the usual grapes. The honest, unpretentious pour for any hour in Beaune, and the proper base of a Kir Royale. Where every cellar · every list

old.name: Marc & Fine de Bourgogne
old.label: SPIRIT
old.hook: Two Burgundy brandies — one from the pomace, one from the lees
old.text: Two Burgundy brandies — one from the pomace, one from the lees EUR 6-14 / glass WALK-IN Digestif Marc de Bourgogne is distilled from the pressed grape skins and stalks; Fine de Bourgogne from the wine lees, the sediment left in the barrel — finer, rounder, oak-aged a minimum of three years. Both were raised to full AOC in 2011, set on a par with Cognac and Armagnac. The Marc is also what washes the rind of an Époisses. The digestif to end a Beaune dinner. Where after dinner

drink:Marc and Fine de Bourgogne.brief: Verify the AOC/IG dates (old: Marc 1942, Fine 2011 — these look shaky; the EU geographical indications for spirits: verify, else soften). Wine labels.

old.name: Marché aux Vins at opening — 10:00
old.label: GEM
old.text: The former Cordeliers church takes its first visitors at 10:00 into cool stone chapels with almost nobody else present. The self-guided tasting circuit can be walked in 45 minutes at that hour in something close to silence — five wines, three intact Gothic chapels, the day not yet arrived. Where Centre When 10:00 on a weekday

old_record.name: Bouchard Père & Fils
old_record.why: Cellars inside a 15th-century royal fortress. To order: the guided fortress-cellar visit and tasting; the Beaune Grèves 'Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus'. Bouchard took the Château de Beaune — built for Louis XI — in 1820; the cellars run 10 m into the rampart, holding 19th-century bottles. Book ahead; tours Tue–Sat.

old_record.why: The largest cellars in Burgundy — 5 km of galleries. To order: the self-guided cellar visit with a tasting of 6 wines, 25 €. Founded 1780, the galleries dug under a former Visitandine convent — around two million bottles ageing in the dark. The clearest sense of how much wine sleeps beneath Beaune. Verify hours before going.
